authority: SQLite is the controlled migration source for legacy application records; protected Saved Data resource files are the target production authority while authentication remains protected SQLite

rules.cutoverRule: Import only through the protected Badminton administrator path. Compare with the current server state and never let a browser copy silently overwrite a newer shared revision.

The protected shared Badminton resource is authoritative after cutover. Clear or refresh the local cache only after a verified server load and enforce established Badminton administration permissions.

Created only when the browser and protected shared resource conflict. Never auto-import or auto-delete it; an administrator must compare it with the authoritative revision before resolving the backup.

The complete Diet Log document (logs, notes, saved recipes and health/profile fields) is preserved as a browser import candidate after an authenticated server read. It may become account data only after the signed-in user explicitly chooses Import browser Diet Log, including when the authoritative server resource is empty at revision 0. Bind an unresolved legacy candidate to the first authenticated account that reviews it so account switching cannot offer the same candidate to another account. Delete the legacy key only after verified server acceptance or an explicit keep-account decision.

This metadata does not contain Diet Log content. It binds the unresolved global legacy Diet Log candidate to the first authenticated account that reviews it, preventing the same candidate from being offered after an account switch. Remove it only with the associated legacy source after verified import or Keep account.
Created on a stale or divergent Food save. Never auto-retry with a newly fetched revision and never delete the backup until the authoritative account document has been reviewed.
Deletion-only compatibility state. It is not user content and must not become permanent Saved Data.

For a signed-in user, Users/{paddedUserId}/voice.json is authoritative, including an empty resource which resolves to account defaults. The browser key remains only guest/file-mode preference state and must never be automatically promoted into an authenticated account or used as authenticated save fallback.

Treat this as an individual game save, never Shared Badminton. A signed-in user must explicitly adopt/import the local profile for this game; an existing server save is never replaced automatically and all server mutations use expectedRevision.
Treat v1 as the current primary and v2 as the compatibility copy. Report a conflict if their payloads differ; do not choose silently.
This controls device-specific automatic round progression and is not account progression.
Split by recognised game ID using canonicalGameFiles. Require a signed-in user decision and stale-write comparison; guest data must never automatically replace authenticated progress.
Prefer an existing authenticated Games Hub profile. Import local data only after recognised-resource validation, revision comparison and conflict review.
Recipe titles are regenerated from page content and are not the favourites authority.

For a signed-in user, account profile state is authoritative, including an empty profile. Quarantine any pre-existing browser profile under an account-scoped recovery key before the application reads it. After server load, expose a deliberate Import browser copy or Keep account copy decision; imports use the current fitness expectedRevision and server schema validation. Never derive Saved Data paths from the username embedded in a browser key.
Generic wrapper calls are accounted for by the concrete keys passed into them.

This is the Meridian Grove Exploration game save. The Games Hub guard maps the key to the isolated meridiangrove game profile, whose canonical physical file is meridian-grove.json. Keep it separate from the Baseline Realm ninja envelope and require the standard explicit per-game browser import with expectedRevision protection.

For a signed-in user, the authoritative account routine is loaded first, including an empty routine. A different meaningful browser routine/log copy is preserved as an import candidate and may become account data only after the user explicitly chooses Import browser copy with the current expectedRevision. Keeping the account copy removes the old physical browser source; authenticated compatibility reads are virtualised from account state.

For a signed-in user, the authoritative account groups/assignments are loaded first, including an empty section. A different meaningful browser copy is preserved as an import candidate and may become account data only after the user explicitly chooses Import browser copy with the shared skincare expectedRevision. Keeping the account copy removes the old physical browser source; unrelated skincare sections must remain preserved.

For a signed-in user, authoritative account slider state is loaded first, including an empty slider set. A different browser slider copy is preserved as an import candidate and may be merged only after the user explicitly chooses Import browser copy, only in mirror or saved-data mode, and only with expectedRevision. Keeping the account copy removes the old browser source.
These are recovery copies created only on divergence or revision conflict. Never auto-import, retry or delete them until the authoritative resource has been reviewed.
The current start-day/display preference affects calendar presentation rather than persistent routine content and remains device-local.

For a signed-in user, account active-workout state is authoritative, including no active workout. Quarantine a pre-existing browser workout before application startup and expose it only as an explicit import candidate. Import only after the user chooses Import browser copy and only when plan ID, current session and step validation succeed with the current fitness expectedRevision; invalid, stale or conflicting entries must remain preserved and must not be silently applied.
These known bridge lookup keys are already covered by the separate Fitness cache and file-protocol fallback decisions. They create no additional browser resource.

This recovery copy is created before an authenticated legacy Fitness browser key is removed from its active application location. Keep it until an explicit import succeeds or the user chooses Keep account copy. Never auto-import it and never expose it across account names.
The server plan is authoritative during migration; this cache may only accelerate display and must be replaced after a verified authoritative read.
Production uses the protected Fitness API. This fallback must not compete with SQLite during migration or the Saved Data resource after cutover.

For a signed-in user, the Baseline Realm tacticalOperations section is authoritative even when absent/empty. Preserve this v1 browser copy only as an explicit import candidate when no equivalent account state exists. Never promote it automatically; remove it only after the user chooses Keep account copy or a later authoritative account load verifies an imported equivalent state.

For a signed-in user, the Baseline Realm inventory-service tacticalOperations section is authoritative even when absent/empty. A divergent v2 browser copy must be presented for Import browser copy or Keep account copy and must never be loaded as account state automatically. Keep the browser recovery copy until a later authoritative account load verifies the imported equivalent.
Current tab or view is not progression data.
Do not persist as account data.
Never migrate browser-stored password material or treat this preview fallback as an account source.
Authenticated server sessions remain authoritative; do not migrate this local preview session.
This temporary route handoff exists only while replacing a standalone recipe shell with the complete parent application. Never migrate it to Saved Data.
This remembers only the selected My Body subtab for the current browser session and is not Fitness account data.

These values remember only the selected My Routine page or Fitness Plan subtab for the current browser session. They are navigation state, not routine content or account data, and must never become Saved Data resources.
